subject: Protracted response lag impacting checkout (Finexia)
messages:
From: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@finexia.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finexia.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T18:10:00Z
Subject: Protracted response lag impacting checkout (Finexia)

Karthik —

We started seeing elevated checkout failures and timeouts across multiple regions starting ~17:45 UTC on 2027-09-04. Summary from our side: p95 stays ~400ms but the p99 and p999 bins grew to ~8–18s for some requests; downstream systems started timing out so we saw ~2.6% 5xx during the window and a 7% drop in completed checkouts for the hour. Attached is a histogram extracted from our monitoring (finexia_checkout_spike_histogram.csv) and a short synthetic run we did with k6 (k6-synthetic-run-20270904.pdf).

Important details:
- Affected routes: /api/checkout/submit and /api/cart/validate (eu-west and us-west primarily)
- Error types: 503 gateway errors and several customer-facing timeouts (frontend JS shows 10s client timeout)
- Start: ~2027-09-04T17:45:00Z, intermittent beyond 19:10Z

We need an urgent root-cause readout and a plan to stop the bleed. Can you set up a bridge and share initial observations? If you need any extra logs from our side we can provide request IDs — sample request IDs in attachment.

This is impacting our Black Friday prep tests; customer success and finance are already asking. Appreciate quick cadence.

— Aisha
Aisha Gomez
Head of Platform | Finexia
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@finexia.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finexia.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T18:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Protracted response lag impacting checkout (Finexia)

Aisha — thank you for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We’re pulling traces and service metrics now. Initial plan:

1) Rapid triage call tomorrow 2027-09-05 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT (I’ll send a calendar invite) — engineering + CS + Finexia platform.
2) We’ll collect a request sample list (please confirm 10 sample request IDs to correlate) and I’ve asked dev to pull server-side request traces + worker metrics for the timeframe.
3) Short-term mitigation: if we confirm queueing backlog or concurrency surface, we’ll apply a targeted routing policy to route Finexia traffic to a variant with higher concurrency and disable aggressive batching for the affected routes.

I’ve cc’d Dev (runtime) and Marissa (CS/AM) to coordinate. Laura, Hannah — please start a lightweight RCA doc and capture immediate hypotheses (throttles, KV cache fragmentation, ingress bursts). I’ll escalate to the on-call SRE if we see >2% 5xx sustained.

— Karthik

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T19:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Protracted response lag impacting checkout (Finexia) — preliminary traces

Quick notes from the runtime side (preliminary):

- I pulled request traces from 2027-09-04T17:30–19:30Z. Two correlated signals stand out:
  * elevated queue_wait_time_ms on worker pool A (us-west region) — spikes up to ~14.5s in the heavy tail for certain requests. Example log snippet: "INFO [worker] request_id=finx-abc123 queue_wait_time_ms=14500 worker_id=w-42"
  * a subset of requests shows repeated KV cache misses followed by a small burst of rehydration work that temporarily ties up a small number of GPU workers (observed via our internal latency heatmap).

- Concurrency controls: we have a soft cap configured per-tenant for safety; Finexia’s route had a conservative per-worker concurrency limit set in the routing policy which combined with a sudden 2x traffic burst created localized queuing on that pool. When the backlog peaked, we observed longer-than-expected prefix recomputation tasks that held the worker for ~7–12s before completions resumed.

- Error rate: the 503s appear to be gateway-level timeouts when the router gave up after the configured upstream deadline (10s). So the chain is: traffic burst -> backlog -> worker held for long-running cache rehydrate -> queue wait grows -> router times out -> 5xxs exposed to Finexia.

Attachments: I uploaded a compressed trace bundle to the shared drive (request-traces-20270904.zip). I also exported a small CSV with per-request wait times (finexia_checkout_spike_histogram.csv).

Hypotheses to test on the call:
- Batching/windowing interaction with conservative per-tenant concurrency -> amplifier effect under bursts
- Slow prefix recompute due to larger-than-expected prompt sizes for some customer calls
- Edge case in KV cache eviction that serializes rehydration onto GPU worker main thread

Immediate mitigations I can run after approval on the call: bump tenant concurrency on the affected pool by 40% for 30 minutes and lock the routing fallback to a pre-warmed variant. If that fixes it we can follow with a safepoint rollback plan.

— Dev

Looping in a quick customer-facing update I’ll share post-call. Aisha, Tom — Finexia is understandably nervous given their upcoming volume tests; they’ve asked for a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes timeline for mitigation, a statement of impact, and potential goodwill consideration. I’ve drafted a MAP (attached: MAP-Finexia-20270905.docx) with the following ask to internal team:

- Confirm mitigation window and owner (engineering lead + SRE)
- Provide a short note on estimated number of failed checkouts and tentative credit exposure if we offer a service credit (ballpark needed for CS + finance)
- Leader-level readout for execs if we cannot stabilize within 3 hours of mitigation start.

We should be prepared for a request for partial credits if the customer deems the degradation significant for their scheduled tests. Please confirm owners and I’ll send the customer-facing note after the call.

Date: 2027-09-05T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Protracted response lag impacting checkout (Finexia) — post-mitigation action items

Short post-bridge summary and action items (for exec readout):

Summary: We confirmed the primary vector was localized queuing driven by a conservative per-tenant concurrency cap combined with an unusual pattern of KV cache rehydration that serialized work on a small subset of workers. Temporary mitigation (bumped concurrency + pinned routing to warmed variant) reduced queue_wait_time_ms and dropped 5xx to <0.2% within 9 minutes. Finexia validated reduced failures in their synthetic checks.

Action items (owners):
- Engineering (Dev) — run a short config experiment: adjust tenant concurrency heuristics to be traffic-sensitive for 48 hours and monitor for regressions. Collect full trace of rehydrate path. (owner: dev_patel)
- Platform (Karthik) — prepare an exec one-pager documenting root cause, mitigation timeline, and credit exposure estimate. (owner: karthik_iyer)
- CS (Marissa) — finalize MAP and proposed credit language; share with Finexia. (owner: marissa_cole)
- SRE (Hannah) — add alert for rapid rise in queue_wait_time_ms for any tenant above the configured threshold. (owner: hannah_schmitt)

If credit exposure estimate exceeds $25k we will escalate to revenue ops and schedule an executive sync. I’ll put a short readout in the 24-hour exec digest.

Thanks team — please add notes to the shared RCA doc and tag any reproducible traces.

— Laura
